request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: an explainable boosting machine (EBM), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (5,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 31.7% (95% band 26.3% to 39.9%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.4; 1: +0.5; >= 2: +2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.43, 95% band [+2.18, +2.63]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 21.3% (95% band 18.0% to 26.9%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 104999: +0.4; 105000-344999: -0.17; >= 345000: -1 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -1.28, 95% band [-1.83, -1.07]).
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 9.8% (95% band 4.0% to 13.0%); rank 3 to 7 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.24, 95% band [-0.60, +0.19]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 9.4% (95% band 4.0% to 13.6%); rank 3 to 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): falls by 0.44 (95% band [-0.71, -0.13]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 16,500 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 7.9% (95% band 2.6% to 11.1%); rank 3 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.70 (95% band [+0.15, +1.15]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 198,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 5.5% (95% band 1.7% to 9.1%); rank 4 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.13, 95% band [-0.10, +0.44]).
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 3.1% (95% band 0.9% to 6.7%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.33 (95% band [+0.01, +0.57]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 191,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 2.0% (95% band 0.1% to 6.0%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.10 (95% band [+0.00, +0.27]) from x = 1 (5th percentile) to x = 3 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 1.9% (95% band 0.7% to 5.9%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.23, 95% band [-0.60, +0.03]).

Interactions: the model has 5 pairs. The larger ones:
- `BILL_AMT1 & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 1.9% (95% band 0.0% to 2.5%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 198,000: +0.98 (95% band +0.15 to +1.37) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +0.43 (95% band +0.13 to +1.02) when `PAY_AMT2` = 17,400.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 17,400: -0.17 (95% band -0.61 to +0.29) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.72 (95% band -0.86 to +0.12) when `BILL_AMT1` = 198,000.
- `BILL_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 1.9% (95% band 0.0% to 3.6%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 198,000: +0.53 (95% band +0.15 to +1.22) when `AGE` = 23, +0.51 (95% band -0.03 to +1.02) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.21 (95% band -0.09 to +0.61) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, +0.19 (95% band -0.41 to +0.33) when `BILL_AMT1` = 198,000.
- `AGE & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 1.5% (95% band 0.0% to 2.2%).
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.20 (95% band -0.14 to +0.53) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -0.13 (95% band -0.39 to +0.31) when `BILL_AMT2` = 191,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 191,000: +0.44 (95% band +0.00 to +0.63) when `AGE` = 23, +0.11 (95% band -0.17 to +0.50) when `AGE` = 53.
- `AGE & PAY_AMT3`: share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.0% to 1.7%).
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.09 (95% band -0.13 to +0.43) when `PAY_AMT3` = 0, +0.20 (95% band -0.18 to +0.45) when `PAY_AMT3` = 17,300.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT3` from 0 to 17,300: -0.26 (95% band -0.58 to +0.02) when `AGE` = 23, -0.16 (95% band -0.53 to +0.08) when `AGE` = 53.
- `PAY_AMT2 & AGE`: share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.0% to 2.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 17,400: -0.20 (95% band -0.68 to +0.24) when `AGE` = 23, -0.08 (95% band -0.59 to +0.23) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.02 (95% band -0.21 to +0.43) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +0.14 (95% band -0.28 to +0.45) when `PAY_AMT2` = 17,400.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven most strongly by the repayment status in September 2005, the latest month: applicants who paid in full or were only one month late have a noticeably lower predicted risk, while applicants with two or more months of payment delay carry a much higher predicted risk, a swing of roughly 2.4 units on the log-odds scale."},{"id":2,"text":"The second most important driver is the size of the credit limit: smaller credit lines (under about 105,000 NT dollars) are associated with higher predicted risk, and very large lines (345,000 NT dollars or more) are associated with lower predicted risk."},{"id":3,"text":"Several other factors matter less and are less certain: the amounts paid in September and August 2005 each show a modest downward effect on risk, and the September bill amount shows an upward effect, but the shape of these effects between their extremes is not settled by the data."},{"id":4,"text":"Age and the July payment amount show no effect that the data can distinguish from zero, and education has at most a small upward effect on risk that is itself uncertain."},{"id":5,"text":"The model contains several interactions, but each is small and its uncertainty range includes zero, so the data do not establish that the effect of any feature depends meaningfully on another."},{"id":6,"text":"The one interaction worth noting is between the September bill amount and the August payment: the rise in predicted risk from a larger September bill appears to be smaller when the August payment is larger, though this pattern is not reliably established."},{"id":7,"text":"Overall, the predictions rest mainly on recent repayment behaviour and the size of the credit line, with the remaining features contributing less and with more uncertainty about their effects."}]}
